The supplied parent construction has at least one worst lag near the target upper bound, and recent improvements for this problem are usually obtained by delicately rebalancing the active set of finite-support overlap lags with fractional values near the suggested parent rather than by a coarse global search. The plan therefore uses a fixed dimension derived from the supplied parent (normally the supplied 63-point construction, unless invalid), because that resolution is already aligned with the best-known local structure and is small enough to make every heuristic evaluation inexpensive. The primary reducer is a deterministic/stochastic suite of three local/near-local engines operating on the same exactly feasible box/simplex constraint:

- a logarithmic soft-max smoothing of the true overlap objective plus a feasibility-projected gradient (and an optional SLSQP variant) to descend the max without nonsmooth ambiguity;
- an exact active/protective-lag trust-region linearization, solved as a genuine linear program and accepted only after exact nonsmooth evaluation, to push down multiple active lags at once;
